name: Luxembourg
summary_text: Luxembourg is exceptionally safe — one of Europe's strongest trans jurisdictions. Legal gender recognition by self-determination since 2018 (Act of 10 August 2018), with no medical requirements, and notably the process is open to foreign nationals as well as citizens. Discrimination on grounds of sexual orientation and gender identity is banned across employment, goods, services, education, and health; a national LGBTI action plan has operated since 2018; an equality body (CET) handles complaints. No traveler-facing concerns exist: no bathroom laws, no border issues (Schengen), no documented anti-trans violence pattern. Gaps are minor: no nonbinary marker, and gender expression/sex characteristics are not explicitly covered in anti-discrimination law.

sources.title: Applying to change one's gender status and first name(s) in the civil register - Guichet.lu - Luxembourg
sources.claim_summary: Official Luxembourg government portal (Guichet.lu) page on applying to change one's gender status and first name(s) in the civil register - the administrative procedure for legal gender recognition.

sources.title: Luxembourg | Outright International
sources.claim_summary: Outright International country overview (updated March 2026): marriage and adoption; self-determination-based gender markers (no nonbinary markers); discrimination banned on sexual orientation and gender identity but not gender expression or sex characteristics; no measures on conversion practices or intersex interventions; in July 2025 the government unveiled a comprehensive LGBTIQ+ Action Plan, criticised by organisations for missing depathologisation and other key elements.

Centre LGBTIQ+ Cigale UPR submission (April 2023) for Luxembourg: describes the organisation's services and Luxembourg's equality laws (employment, goods and services, education, health), the CET equality body and the national LGBTI action plan.

sources.title: LGBTQ+ Travel Safety Index: 203 Countries Ranked in 2023
sources.claim_summary: Asher Fergusson's LGBTQ+ Travel Safety Index (updated June 2023): 400+ hours of research ranking all countries' laws for LGBTQ+ traveller safety, with a companion Global Transgender Rights Index - comparative data source covering Luxembourg.

sources.title: Agressions LGBTphobes : un durcissement des sanctions attendu
sources.claim_summary: Le Quotidien (June 2019, in French): 'Agressions LGBTphobes: un durcissement des sanctions attendu' - Luxembourg law lacks LGBTphobic aggravating circumstances; victims under-report; the justice minister signalled the law would evolve after ECRI's 2017 intervention.

sources.title: Personnes transgenres et intersexes : l'état civil laissera le choix de l'identité
sources.claim_summary: Le Quotidien (May 2017, in French): Justice Minister Félix Braz presented a bill allowing trans and intersex people to change civil-status gender by declaration - replacing the long, costly judicial procedure; welcomed by associations.

sources.title: Chambre : Changement d'état civil simplifié pour les personnes transgenres
sources.claim_summary: Le Quotidien (July 2018, in French): the Chamber approved bill 7146 simplifying gender and first-name changes for trans people (57-3, only ADR opposed) - change by written request with supporting documents, no medical requirements.
